what_its_for: Gilteritinib is a cancer medicine used to treat a type of blood cancer called acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in adults whose cancer has come back or did not respond to other treatments. It works specifically in patients whose cancer cells have a certain gene change called an FLT3 mutation. Your doctor will test your blood or bone marrow to make sure this medicine is right for you.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. Try to take it at the same time every day. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet. If you vomit after taking your dose, do not take another dose that day — just wait until your next scheduled dose. Drink plenty of water unless your doctor tells you otherwise.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 120 mg (one tablet) taken by mouth once daily. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how your body responds to the medicine or if you have certain side effects. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been less than 12 hours since your scheduled time, take it as soon as you remember. If it has been more than 12 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time the following day. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store gilteritinib tablets at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container and away from moisture, heat, and direct sunlight. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to safely dispose of any leftover tablets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, and St. John's Wort while taking this medicine, as they can change the amount of medicine in your body. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting gilteritinib, because many medications can interact with it. Avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medicine — use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 6 months after your last dose. Men should use condoms during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: chest pain, fast or irregular heartbeat, shortness of breath, or swelling in your legs or feet (signs of heart problems); severe muscle pain or weakness, dark-colored urine, or feeling very tired (signs of a muscle breakdown condition called posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or rhabdomyolysis); confusion, seizures, vision changes, or headaches; fever, chills, or signs of infection; unusual bleeding or bruising; severe nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that does not stop; yellowing of the skin or eyes; or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: It may take several weeks before you notice improvements, and your doctor will monitor your blood counts and other lab tests regularly to check how the medicine is working. Do not stop taking gilteritinib without talking to your doctor, even if you feel well, because stopping too early can allow the cancer to come back.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine can harm an unborn baby. Do not use if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Women of childbearing age must use effective contraception during treatment and for 6 months after stopping. Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment. Liver problems: If you have moderate or severe liver disease, your doctor may need to monitor you more closely or adjust your dose. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects and should be monitored carefully. Always tell your doctor about all your health conditions before starting this medicine.
